title: InputEvent.is_echo() is always false with Fcitx5 IME
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in v4.6.3.stable and v4.7.stable



### System information

CachyOS Linux SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Thu, 01 Oct 2026 21:20:21 +0000 on Wayland - KDE Plasma 6.7.5 - Wayland display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT (RADV GFX1201) - AMD Ryzen 7 9700X 8-Core Processor (16 threads) - 30.94 GiB memory - PulseAudio (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

In Linux/BSD, when input is being passed through Fcitx5 using Wayland's text-input protocol, `InputEvent.is_echo()` always returns false, regardless on whether key input repetition is actually occurring or not via a key being held.

This may also happen with other IMEs such as IBus, but this hasn't been tested yet.

#### Workarounds

Setting the environment variable `SDL_IM_MODULE=fcitx` corrects this. Since this is a local setting rather than something that can be packaged in a build, this can't be considered a full fix.

### Steps to reproduce

- Set Fcitx5 as an IME (in Plasma it can be set as a Virtual Keyboard through System Settings > Input & Output > Keyboard > Virtual Keyboard)
- Run Godot editor under Wayland (either by running `godot --display-driver wayland` or setting the Editor setting  "Run>Platforms>Linux/BSD>Prefer Wayland")
- Run the MRP and hold any key. It should print the event that's occurred and whether it's an echo event on the console.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[echo_bug.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33225048/echo_bug.zip)
